messages.author: 2502c952822e4f47
messages.subject: dropping markers with a defined RF
parts:
Dear all,

I have a linkage map from which I wish to remove markers which have a recombination fraction less than my defined threshold.

I am able to pull out the matrix using the pull.rf command, but I do not know how to proceed further.

I understand that I could use drop.markers, but how can I extract the list of markers from the matrix?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: Re: dropping markers with a defined RF
parts:
Hi SKY - you have two options. 
1) If your are able to estimate your genetic map, the best approach is to use: pickMarkerSubset. This lets you weight markers by missing data etc. and choose the best ones in a given interval. For example, if you set

min.distance = 2, you will only retain the best marker in every 2cM window. It is a bit tricky to use though. There is also qtlTools:repPickMarkerSubset which makes it a bit more user friendly. For example:

> culled.cross = repPickMarkerSubset(orig.cross, min.distance = 2) # creates a new cross object with only a single marker in every 2 cM window.


2) Alternatively, if your genotype matrix is too big to estimate a map (>~10k markers), you can cull by the recombination fractions chromosome-by-chromosome using qtlTools::dropSimilarMarkers. This employs the protocol you describe above - find and cull markers that have low recombination fractions. You can define your recombination fraction threshold via the rf.threshold argument. However, this approach does not perform quite as well as scanning across the map via pickMarkerSubset since it is agnostic to the order of markers. 
Good luck,
John
